decision_rule: Ask for municipality and neighborhood before selecting BMLWE NLWE SLWE or BWE.
examples: user says water is cut in my area but gives no location
notes: Water establishment routing is location-dependent and runtime municipality map is required.

decision_rule: Do not route to WE unless complaint identifies public meter public source public pipe or shared network issue.
examples: apartment leak; rooftop tank; private pump; internal pipes
notes: Official mandates cover public water services and networks not internal private plumbing.

decision_rule: Route pipe repair to WE and public-space restoration to municipality or MPWT depending road class.
examples: burst pipe undermining road; water leak creating pothole
notes: Use HITL when road class is unknown or safety risk exists.

decision_rule: Classify storm drain local road drainage sewer overflow and emergency flooding before routing.
examples: rainwater pooling; manhole overflow; sewage smell in street
notes: WE only when evidence points to wastewater sewer or water network.

decision_rule: Emergency response first then technical follow-up with infrastructure owner.
examples: sewage entering home; flood trapped people; collapse risk
notes: Use emergency entity first where rescue or immediate danger exists.

decision_rule: Route to WE and add public-health or environmental escalation when source suggests contamination beyond network.
examples: brown tap water in neighborhood; river pollution near source
notes: BWE and EBML official pages support quality-monitoring role. Environmental or Litani-basin source pollution needs HITL.

decision_rule: Keep WE as citizen-facing water service route unless complaint is purely electricity grid fault.
examples: water pumps not running because power outage
notes: Do not send water outage directly to EDL unless the citizen reports only an electrical grid issue.

decision_rule: Confirm asset owner before routing. LRA may be primary for Litani-related irrigation assets.
examples: blocked irrigation canal; Qasimiya canal issue; Ras Al Ain irrigation
notes: SLWE official overview explicitly notes irrigation exception assigned to LRA under Article 7. LRA contact page confirms Qasimiya and Ras Al Ain office contacts.

decision_rule: Use BWE when the issue is within BWE ordinary service scope and no LRA asset evidence exists.
examples: farm irrigation subscription; Bekaa irrigation water complaint
notes: BWE official mandate includes irrigation but LRA basin projects require boundary check.

decision_rule: Do not promise prior notice or restoration time. Explain official no-prior-notice categories if relevant.
examples: sudden network failure; local pollution; emergency repair
notes: BWE FAQ lists no-prior-notice cutoff cases.

decision_rule: Prior notice may apply but no generic restoration SLA is published.
examples: planned maintenance; line cleaning; rationing program
notes: BWE FAQ lists prior-notice cutoff categories.

decision_rule: Use MEW only for policy oversight or escalation after the regional WE is identified.
examples: complaint about WE non-response; water-sector policy question
notes: MEW supervises sector but is not first-line field dispatch for ordinary complaints. Claims form is ministry-level oversight not emergency intake.

decision_rule: Route public network water complaints to WE but regulatory well-license tracking to MEW workflow.
examples: private well license; groundwater well permit; license request tracking
notes: MEW has an official groundwater well license tracking page. Keep HITL if complaint is about illegal extraction pollution or basin impacts.
